notes: Core AppCAT execution could not fully analyze legacy WebApplication targets in this Linux environment; fact documents were generated from source inspection.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Password
security.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: `Web.config` defines a database connection string inline with a password segment (`connectionString=...;user id=root;******;database=...`). This is a hard-coded password pattern in application configuration.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
security.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: Database credentials are embedded directly in `Web.config` connection string configuration, indicating static credential storage in source-controlled configuration.

security.title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
security.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

evidence.explanation: User-controlled data is written to HTML output without explicit encoding. In `JobSeeker/Register.aspx.cs` line 60, username input is embedded directly into `lblMsg.Text` with HTML markup. In `JobSeeker/Profile.aspx.cs` line 42 onward, profile fields loaded from database are directly assigned to label text controls. This creates stored/reflected XSS risk if malicious script payloads are persisted in user fields.
